content: Semantic similarity and association overlap to some degree, but do not coincide BIBREF37, BIBREF38. In fact, there exist plenty of pairs that are intuitively associated but not similar. Pairs where the converse is true can also be encountered, although more rarely. An example are synonyms where a word is common and the other infrequent, such as to seize and to commandeer. BIBREF14 revealed that while similarity measures based on the WordNet graph BIBREF39 and human judgments of association in the University of South Florida Free Association Database BIBREF40 do correlate, a number of pairs follow opposite trends. Several studies on human cognition also point in the same direction. For instance, semantic priming can be triggered by similar words without association BIBREF41. On the other hand, a connection with cue words is established more quickly for topically related words rather than for similar words in free association tasks BIBREF42.
